title: Heat Stress, Hydration, PPE and Emergency Response

content.overview: Outdoor, greenhouse and PPE-intensive work can create heat stress. Prevention requires planning, hydration, rest, shade or cooling, training and early response to symptoms rather than relying on worker toughness or thirst alone.

vocabulary.definition: Total heat burden placed on the body from environment, work intensity and clothing or PPE.
Physiological adaptation that develops with repeated controlled exposure to heat.
A range of heat-related medical conditions that can become severe or life-threatening.

sections.title: Heat risk is predictable
sections.body: Air temperature, humidity, radiant heat, workload and PPE all contribute to risk. Work plans should account for these factors before the shift begins.

sections.title: Hydration and recovery must be available
sections.body: Workers should have access to water and appropriate breaks, including shade or cool recovery areas during high heat. Waiting for severe thirst or symptoms is not a prevention plan.

sections.title: Training must include response
sections.body: Workers should recognize heat-illness warning signs, know how to seek help and understand emergency procedures. New or returning workers may need extra acclimatization protection.

workedExamples: A greenhouse shift that is safe at dawn may become hazardous by afternoon as solar load increases; reassess conditions through the day.
Chemical PPE can add heat burden, so application scheduling should consider both label requirements and heat exposure.
commonMistakes: Using thirst as the only hydration trigger.
Assuming experienced workers cannot develop heat illness.
Ignoring the extra heat burden of PPE.
content.practicalApplication: Before hot work, identify forecast and internal conditions, workload, PPE and available recovery areas. Define hydration/rest practices and make emergency response expectations clear to everyone involved.
content.summary: Heat safety requires active management. Environment, workload, PPE, hydration, rest and emergency readiness all belong in the work plan.
